beginner.summary: For software engineers, data engineers and analysts who can write Python and SQL but have not built vector search before. Covers what embeddings are and how text embedding models are chosen, distance metrics and normalisation, exact k-nearest-neighbour search with NumPy, chunking documents, storing and querying vectors in PostgreSQL with pgvector, retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR, nDCG), the ideas behind approximate search (LSH, IVF and HNSW), metadata filtering, BM25 keyword search, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, cross-encoder reranking, vector fields in OpenSearch, Elasticsearch and Redis, ingestion with upserts, memory sizing and a small search API, ending with a hybrid FAQ search capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3 scripts using lists, dictionaries, functions and pip-installed packages, and can read NumPy array code
Writes basic SQL SELECT, INSERT and WHERE statements against PostgreSQL or another relational database
Has a laptop with 16 GB RAM, Docker, Python 3.11 or later and about 10 GB of free disk for models and datasets
outcomes: Embed text with an open embedding model and run exact and approximate nearest-neighbour search with the correct distance metric
Store, index and query vectors with pgvector, OpenSearch, Elasticsearch and Redis, including metadata filters
Measure retrieval quality with recall@k, MRR and nDCG@10 and measure ANN quality against exact ground truth
Build a hybrid search service that fuses BM25 and vector results with RRF and reranks them with a cross-encoder
